dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:401.text: A thorn, 茦. Formed from 艸, with 刺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:402.text: The plant 鼎蕫. Formed from 艸, with 童 indicating the sound. Du Lin says: lotus root.

shuowen:403.text: The plant 狗毒. Formed from 艸, with 繫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:404.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 嫂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:405.text: The medicinal plant called 地黃 (rehmannia). Formed from 艸, with 下 indicating the sound. The cited ritual food text specifies different herbs served with beef, mutton and pork. [Classical witnesses differ over the precise mutton-herb reading.]

shuowen:406.text: The plant 白薟. Formed from 艸, with 僉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:407.text: The plant 黃菳. Formed from 艸, with 金 indicating the sound.

shuowen:408.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 今 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Eating the 芩 of the wild.”

shuowen:409.text: The plant 鹿藿. Formed from 艸, with 麃 indicating the sound. Read like 剽. Another explanation: a kind of 𦳋.

shuowen:410.text: The plant 綬. Formed from 艸, with 鶪 indicating the sound. This is the term in the Odes: “On the mound there is fine 𧅖.”

shuowen:411.text: Water caltrop, 芰. Formed from 艸, with 淩 indicating the sound. Chu calls it 芰; Qin calls it 薢茩.

shuowen:412.text: Water caltrop, 蔆. Formed from 艸, with 支 indicating the sound.

shuowen:413.text: The plant 薢茩. Formed from 艸, with 解 indicating the sound.

shuowen:414.text: The plant 薢茩. Formed from 艸, with 后 indicating the sound.

shuowen:415.text: The plant 雞頭. Formed from 艸, with 欠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:416.text: The plant 日精, flowering in autumn. Formed from 艸, with abbreviated 𥶶 indicating the sound. Its pronunciation is given by 居六 fanqie.

shuowen:417.text: The plant 爵麥. Formed from 艸, with 龠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:418.text: Male 茅 grass. Formed from 艸, with 遬 indicating the sound. 遬 is the large-seal form of 速.

shuowen:419.text: The flowering head of 茅 grass. Formed from 艸, with 私 indicating the sound.

shuowen:420.text: A 雚 reed not yet flowering. Formed from 艸, with 兼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:421.text: The reed 𦵹. Formed from 艸, with 亂 indicating the sound. In the eighth month 薍 becomes 葦.

shuowen:422.text: A 雚 reed first sprouting. Another name is 薍; another is 鵻. Formed from 艸, with 剡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:423.text: The reed 蒹. Formed from 艸, with 廉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:424.text: 青薠, resembling 莎. Formed from 艸, with 煩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:425.text: Sweet flag, 昌蒲, as it is called in Yizhou. Formed from 艸, with 卬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:426.text: The plant 䒢䓉. Formed from 艸, with 邪 indicating the sound.

shuowen:427.text: Reed flowers. Formed from 艸, with 刀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:428.text: Reed flowers, 芀. Formed from 艸, with 𠛱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:429.text: The lotus bud 䓿𧂄. Formed from 艸, with 圅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:430.text: 䓿𧂄: an unopened lotus flower is 䓿𧂄; once open it is 芙蓉. Formed from 艸, with 閻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:431.text: The fruit of the lotus. Formed from 艸, with 連 indicating the sound.

shuowen:432.text: A lotus stem. Formed from 艸, with 加 indicating the sound.

shuowen:433.text: A lotus leaf. Formed from 艸, with 何 indicating the sound.

shuowen:434.text: The base of the lotus. Formed from 艸, with 密 indicating the sound.

shuowen:435.text: A lotus root. Formed from 艸 and 水, with 禺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:436.text: The plant 天蘥. Formed from 艸, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:437.text: A kind of mugwort. After ten years it has a hundred stalks. The Changes uses it for counting. The Son of Heaven's stalks are nine feet long; lords' seven, grandees' five, and scholars' three. Formed from 艸, with 耆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:438.text: Fragrant mugwort. Formed from 艸, with 臤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:439.text: 蘿莪, a kind of mugwort. Formed from 艸, with 我 indicating the sound.

shuowen:440.text: The plant 莪. Formed from 艸, with 羅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:441.text: A kind of mugwort. Formed from 艸, with 林 indicating the sound.

shuowen:442.text: The plant 牡蒿. Formed from 艸, with 𤈫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:443.text: The plant 艾蒿, mugwort. Formed from 艸, with 肅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:444.text: The plant 蕭. Formed from 艸, with 秋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:445.text: The plant 鳧茈. Formed from 艸, with 勺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:446.text: The plant 王彗. Formed from 艸, with 𣾅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:447.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 爲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:448.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 冘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:449.text: The plant 治牆. Formed from 艸, with 鞠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:450.text: 蘠靡, namely 虋冬. Formed from 艸, with 牆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:451.text: The plant 芪母. Formed from 艸, with 氏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:452.text: 茈菀, found in Fangling, Hanzhong. Formed from 艸, with 宛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:453.text: The plant 貝母. Formed from 艸, with abbreviated 明 indicating the sound.

shuowen:454.text: Mountain 薊. Formed from 艸, with 术 indicating the sound.

shuowen:455.text: 析蓂, large 薺. Formed from 艸, with 冥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:456.text: The plant 荎藸. Formed from 艸, with 味 indicating the sound.

shuowen:457.text: 荎藸, a plant. Formed from 艸, with 至 indicating the sound.

shuowen:458.text: The plant 荎藸. Formed from 艸, with 豬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:459.text: A plant used for fine and coarse 葛 cloth. Formed from 艸, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:460.text: A kind of 葛. Formed from 艸, with 曼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:461.text: A kind of 葛 with white flowers. Formed from 艸, with 皐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:462.text: The plant 菨餘. Formed from 艸, with 杏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:463.text: The plant 菨餘. Formed from 艸, with 妾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:464.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 𥊽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:465.text: The plant 魚毒. Formed from 艸, with 元 indicating the sound.

shuowen:466.text: The plant 大苦. Formed from 艸, with 霝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:467.text: The plant 蕛苵. Formed from 艸, with 稊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:468.text: The plant 蕛苵. Formed from 艸, with 失 indicating the sound.

shuowen:469.text: 艼熒, namely 朐. Formed from 艸, with 丁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:470.text: The plant 苽蔣. Formed from 艸, with 將 indicating the sound.

shuowen:471.text: 雕苽, also called 蔣. Formed from 艸, with 瓜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:472.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 育 indicating the sound.

shuowen:473.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 罷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:474.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 難 indicating the sound.

shuowen:475.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 良 indicating the sound.

shuowen:476.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 要 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “In the fourth month 葽 flowers.” Liu Xiang explains: its taste is bitter; it is 苦葽.

shuowen:477.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 過 indicating the sound.

shuowen:478.text: A ground mushroom. Formed from 艸, with 囷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:479.text: Fungus on mulberry trees. Formed from 艸, with 覃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:480.text: Wood-ear fungus. Formed from 艸, with 耎 indicating the sound. Another name is 萮茈.

shuowen:481.text: Mulberry fruit. Formed from 艸, with 甚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:482.text: A fruit. Formed from 艸, with 竘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:483.text: A plant. Another explanation: the tree 芘茮. Formed from 艸, with 比 indicating the sound.

shuowen:484.text: 木堇, whose flowers open in the morning and fall in the evening. Formed from 艸, with 䑞 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “A face like the 蕣 flower.”

shuowen:485.text: The plant 茱萸. Formed from 艸, with 臾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:486.text: 茱萸, a kind of 茮. Formed from 艸, with 朱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:487.text: The plant 茮莍. Formed from 艸, with 尗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:488.text: Clusters of spiny protrusions on the outer surface of the fruits of 茮 and 樧. Formed from 艸, with 求 indicating the sound.

shuowen:489.text: The tree 楚, thorn or vitex. Formed from 艸, with 刑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:490.text: Water's clothing, an aquatic growth. Formed from 艸, with 治 indicating the sound.

shuowen:491.text: A sprout or bud. Formed from 艸, with 牙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:492.text: A plant's sprout. Formed from 艸, with 明 indicating the sound.

shuowen:493.text: The appearance of plants first emerging from the earth. Formed from 艸, with 出 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Those reeds newly sprouting.”

shuowen:494.text: The main stem supporting a plant’s branches. Formed from 艸, with 巠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:495.text: A stalk. Formed from 艸, with 廷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:496.text: Leaves of plants and trees. Formed from 艸, with 枼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:497.text: Small plants. Formed from 艸, with 㓹 indicating the sound. 㓹 is the ancient form of 銳. Read like 芮.

shuowen:498.text: Abundant flowers. Formed from 艸, with 不 indicating the sound. Another explanation: the plant 芣苢.

shuowen:499.text: A flower. Formed from 艸, with 皅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:500.text: The flourishing blossom of a plant. Formed from 艸, with 尹 indicating the sound.
